overview: Two RNA sequencing strategies distinguished by resolution — one profiles gene expression cell-by-cell, the other averages across an entire sample.
genZNote: Bulk RNA-seq gives you the class average. Single-cell RNA-seq gives you every student's individual grade.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Sequences RNA from individual cells separately, revealing cell-to-cell heterogeneity within a sample.
aspects.valueB: Sequences RNA extracted from a pooled population of cells, producing an averaged expression profile.

aspects.label: Resolution
aspects.valueA: Single-cell resolution — can identify distinct cell types and rare subpopulations.
aspects.valueB: Population-averaged — masks heterogeneity between individual cells.

aspects.label: Cost and Technical Complexity
aspects.valueA: More expensive, technically demanding, and generates larger, sparser datasets requiring specialized analysis.
aspects.valueB: Cheaper, simpler workflow, and well-established analysis pipelines.

aspects.label: Sensitivity per Cell
aspects.valueA: Lower sequencing depth per cell, so lowly expressed genes can be harder to detect.
aspects.valueB: Higher sequencing depth overall, giving more robust detection of even lowly expressed transcripts (at the population level).

aspects.label: Typical Use Case
aspects.valueA: Characterizing cellular heterogeneity in tumors, immune profiling, developmental biology.
aspects.valueB: Comparing overall expression differences between conditions/treatments in a tissue or sample.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Resolves gene expression at the individual-cell level.
aspects.valueB: Averages gene expression across an entire cell population.
